ψ.source_text: Google is making its largest single investment in Europe, committing at least €13 billion, roughly $15.1 billion, to AI infrastructure and energy projects in Finland during 2027 and 2028. The plan covers new data center capacity across four locations, including further expansion of Google's long-running Hamina campus. More unusually, Google signed a 22-year agreement with Finnish utility Fortum to purchase up to half of the electricity generated by the Loviisa nuclear plant between 2030 and 2049.
